To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the heavy-ion induced floating gate error annealing is: (i) strongly dependent on the cell feature size, (ii) strongly dependent on LET, and (iii) weakly dependent on the program level of Multi Level Cell (MLC) devices.

1) the annealing rate of the floating gate errors is proportional to the square root of the time; 2) the annealing of floating gate errors is faster in NOR cells than in NAND cells; 3) the annealing is faster for higher LET; 4) the annealing for higher program levels is faster for NOR cells and faster for lower levels in NAND cells.
the annealing time is inversely proportional to the cell size and that the annealing of raw bit errors is faster for higher program levels and for smaller particle LETs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the understanding of the physical mechanisms responsible for the annealing of floating gate errors in Flash memories.
the annealing of floating gate errors after heavy ion irradiation.
the understanding and mitigation of heavy-ion induced Floating Gate errors in NAND and NOR Flash memories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a given LET, the annealing rate of the raw bit errors increases with the cell size, and that, for a fixed cell size, the annealing of the raw bit error is more effective for higher LET.
the room temperature anneal of heavy-ion induced Floating Gate errors is not a simple process, but rather a complicated one, depending on many different parameters.

the annealing of heavy-ion induced errors in Flash memories is a complex phenomenon that is strongly dependent on several parameters, such as the particle LET, the cell feature size and, for Multi level cells, the program level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the annealing of heavy-ion induced Floating Gate errors is a complex phenomenon that is affected by several factors, such as the cell architecture, the feature size, the LET, the threshold voltage distribution, and the program level.

the annealing of heavy-ion induced errors is mainly due to the recovery of charge trapping centers in the tunnel oxide, while the annealing of the cell threshold distribution width is due to the recovery from interface traps in the floating gate oxide.
the annealing time of Floating Gate errors is a function of the LET, the cell feature size and the program level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the annealing of the floating gate error is a very slow process, with timescales ranging from a few hours to several days.
, in the case of NAND Flash, the annealing of raw bit errors is dominated by the evolution of single bit errors.
the annealing of Floating-Gate errors can be exploited in order to mitigate their effect in space applications.
